thread:
alert-bot: :rotating_light: automatic page: prod-eu-west error-rate spike > 5% 5xx (rolling 5m). triggered by http-5xx-rate-alert. avg 502/503 ~6.2% across edge-gateway and inference-gw-eu. paging alice.m and ben-sre.

alice.m (oncall): On it. getting context. is this localized to EU?

ben-sre: seeing a sharp jump at 11:32 UTC. most hits to /v1/completions and /v1/embeddings on inference-gw-eu01. canary fleet (canary-group-42) just finished a rolling deploy ~11:20.

carmen-infra: copying metrics from the dashboard: 
```
error_rate.prod.eu-west (1m): 6.2% (baseline 0.2%)
p50 latency: 120ms -> 160ms
p95 latency: 320ms -> 1.4s
requests/s: stable
```

alice.m (oncall): thanks. tagging deploy-bot — any deploys in last 30m?

deploy-bot: deploy detected: service=inference-gateway, env=prod-eu-west, ref=canary-group-42, started=2026-03-14T11:15:43Z, finished=2026-03-14T11:21:07Z, by=rina-pm

rina-pm: confirmed canary. small config tweak to envoy routing weights (attempt to shift traffic for cache warmup).

ben-sre: hypothesis: envoy routing change caused an unhealthy backend path -> increased 502s from sidecar/proxy. logs show upstream reset errors (connection reset by peer) and a spike in 502s from inference-backend nodes that were part of the canary pool.

opswatch: sample logs (truncated):
```
[2026-03-14T11:25:09Z] inference-gw-eu01 edge: upstream_reset BEFORE_SEND: conn reset (10.10.5.12:443)
[2026-03-14T11:25:09Z] inference-gw-eu01 edge: 502 response for /v1/completions (model: llama-2-13b) req_id=aa1f
[2026-03-14T11:25:10Z] inference-backend-eu-canary-3: worker: kv-cache miss -> reload -> oom? (OOM not observed in container, but worker logs show pod-level stream failure)
```

alice.m (oncall): immediate mitigation options? can we rollback routing change or evacuate canary? we should follow runbook "5xx spike - canary rollback".

carmen-infra: I can flip weights back to previous config for Envoy in prod-eu-west. updating controlplane now.

ben-sre: also proposing to remove canary instances from LB target group to stop sending user traffic (safe, quick). runbook step 2.

alice.m (oncall): do it. call out if any rate-limiting is needed to reduce error noise. also notify customers if impact persists > 15m.

carmen-infra: executing: 
```
# rollback envoy weights
kubectl -n infra exec config-applier -- /bin/sh -c "apply-config --env=prod-eu-west --file=envoy-weights-prev.yaml"
# remove canary pods from target group
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:... --targets Id=i-0abcd1234
```

(2 minutes later)

carmen-infra: change applied. canary targets deregistered. monitoring for drop in 5xx.

ben-sre: after deregister: error_rate -> 0.9% (1m) down from 6.2%. p95 back to ~340ms. looks promising.

alice.m (oncall): nice. leaving page open for verification for next 10m. can we gather a few root-cause indicators: envoy configs diff, canary pod logs, kernel/dmesg for OOMs?

ben-sre: grabbing diffs now. envoy diff shows route weight change from 0.05->0.2 for canary subset and an unexpected header rewrite that caused backend selection to prefer a legacy path with different health probes.

opswatch: pulling canary pod logs: repeated stream resets and HTTP/2 GOAWAY in worker logs.

carmen-infra: no OOMs at node/container level. CPU spiked on canary nodes but not saturated. network RTT slightly higher to backend pool.

alice.m (oncall): looks like config + route weight change pushed some traffic to a backend that fails on HTTP2 stream re-use. good catch. mitigation worked. next steps: 1) create incident ticket + postmortem; 2) revert config in git and block redeploy of canary-group-42 until fix; 3) schedule deep-dive with infra and runtime teams; 4) notify impacted customers if billing/requests lost.

rina-pm: creating incident now: INC-20260314-8342, linking dashboards and diff. will own postmortem.

alice.m (oncall): Ben, please attach logs and envoy diff to the incident. Carmen, confirm deploy block.

ben-sre: attaching logs + example request traces. sample trace id: trace-7c9a.

carmen-infra: setting hold: CI/CD flag set to deny canary-group-42 promotion: 
```
ci-cd lock add canary-group-42 --reason "investigating 5xx spike" --expires 2026-03-15T11:00:00Z
```

opswatch: alert-bot: resolving automatic page since error rate returned to baseline. summarizing: root cause suspected envoy route + header rewrite -> backend path selection -> HTTP/2 stream reset cascade; canary routing increased weight causing higher error surface. mitigation: removed canary from LB and rolled envoy weights back.

alice.m (oncall): marking this thread resolved for oncall. we'll keep incident open for postmortem. good coordination, :thumbsup:.

rina-pm: will post customer impact assessment in incident ticket in 30m. initial estimate: ~12 minutes of elevated errors, ~0.4% of requests in EU affected.

ben-sre: follow-up action items assigned in INC-20260314-8342: (1) revert header rewrite change + add integration test for HTTP/2 stream reuse; (2) add canary throttling guard so new path doesn't exceed X% traffic in 15m; (3) better runbook hooks for auto-deregister on upstream reset spikes.

alice.m (oncall): thanks team. I'll hand off to ben-sre for post-incident verification and to rina-pm for customer comms. paging cleared.

deploy-bot: deploy-block placed on canary-group-42 by carmen-infra.

alert-bot: note: auto-pager will reopen if 5xx > 3% for 5m.

ben-sre: final note: if you want the raw traces and a small script I used to correlate resets -> ping me and I'll drop them in the incident ticket.

rina-pm: thanks all, closing channel for coordination.
